title: Why trigonometric ratios work
keyIdea: Every right triangle with the same acute angle θ has the same three angles, θ, 90° and 90° − θ, so they are all similar. Similar triangles keep their side ratios, so opposite ÷ hypotenuse, adjacent ÷ hypotenuse and opposite ÷ adjacent depend only on θ. Those fixed numbers are sin θ, cos θ and tan θ.

kid: Draw two right triangles with a 35° angle, one small and one big. Both have a third angle of 55°, because the angles add up to 180°.
Same angles means same shape. The big one is a scaled copy of the small one. Every side is multiplied by the same number.
So the fraction opposite ÷ hypotenuse is the same in both. If the big one is twice as big, the top and the bottom both double. 2.87 ÷ 5 and 5.74 ÷ 10 both give 0.574.
That number belongs to the angle, not to the triangle. We call it sin 35°. A calculator knows it for every angle.
adult: Two right triangles that share an acute angle θ have all three angles equal: θ, 90° and 90° − θ. So they are similar (AA). Matching sides share one scale factor k, and a ratio of two sides in one triangle does not change when both are multiplied by k.

That is why sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent are well defined. Each one depends on θ alone. A calculator's sin 35° ≈ 0.574 is that shared ratio, for a triangle of any size.

The names come from where θ is. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The opposite side does not touch θ. The adjacent side touches θ and is not the hypotenuse. Turn the triangle and the names move with θ.

Common mistakes: thinking a bigger triangle has a bigger sine; treating sin θ as proportional to θ (sin 60° ≈ 0.866, not 2 × sin 30° = 1); calling the bottom side adjacent whichever way the triangle faces; writing a ratio upside down, which would make sin or cos bigger than 1; and reading 0.574 as a length instead of a ratio.

familyTip: With a protractor, draw two right triangles that both have a 35° angle, one small and one as big as the page. Measure the side opposite the 35° angle and the longest side of each, then divide. Do both give about 0.57? Check sin 35 on a calculator.

worked.title: Show that sin 35° is the same in right triangles with hypotenuse 5 cm and 12 cm.
steps: Both triangles have angles 35°, 90° and 55°, so they are similar.
Scale factor from the small to the big triangle: k = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.
The small opposite side is about 2.868 cm, so the big one is 2.868 × 2.4 ≈ 6.883 cm.

practice.prompt: Two right triangles share an angle θ. The small one has opposite {o} cm and hypotenuse {h} cm. The big one has hypotenuse {=h*k} cm. How long is its opposite side?
practice.hint: The triangles are similar. The scale factor is {=h*k} ÷ {h}.
practice.explain: k = {k}, so the opposite side is {o} × {k} = {=o*k} cm. The ratio opposite ÷ hypotenuse stays {o}/{h}.

practice.prompt: A right triangle has a 40° angle. What is its third angle?
practice.hint: The three angles add up to 180°, and one of them is 90°.
practice.explain: 180 − 90 − 40 = 50°. Every right triangle with a 40° angle has angles 40°, 50° and 90°, so they are all similar.

practice.prompt: In a right triangle, opposite = {o} and hypotenuse = {h}. A similar triangle is {k} times as big. What is opposite ÷ hypotenuse in the big triangle? Give a decimal.
practice.hint: Both sides are multiplied by {k}. What happens to the fraction?
practice.explain: ({o} × {k}) ÷ ({h} × {k}) = {o} ÷ {h} = {=o/h}. The {k} cancels, so the ratio is unchanged.

practice.prompt: In triangle PQR the right angle is at Q and θ is at P. Which side is opposite θ?
practice.hint: The opposite side is the one that does not touch the corner P.
practice.explain: QR does not touch P, so it is opposite θ. PR is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse, and PQ is adjacent.

practice.hint: Is sin θ proportional to θ? Try it on a calculator.
practice.explain: sin 60° ≈ 0.866. Doubling the angle does not double the ratio, and sin θ can never be more than 1.

pool.prompt: Why is opposite ÷ hypotenuse the same in every right triangle with a 35° angle?
choices: They all have angles 35°, 90° and 55°, so they are similar
They all have the same hypotenuse
The opposite side is always 0.574 cm
pool.hint: What do the angles of these triangles have in common?
pool.explain: Equal angles make the triangles similar. Similar triangles multiply every side by the same factor, so ratios of sides do not change.

pool.prompt: sin 35° ≈ 0.574. A right triangle with a 35° angle has hypotenuse 20 cm. How long is the side opposite the 35° angle, to 1 decimal place?
pool.explain: 20 × 0.574 = 11.48, which is 11.5 cm to 1 decimal place.

pool.prompt: Triangle A has opposite 3 and hypotenuse 5. Triangle B has the same angle θ and hypotenuse 15. Which is true?
choices: B has opposite 9, and both have sin θ = 0.6
B has a bigger sin θ because it is bigger
pool.hint: Find the scale factor 15 ÷ 5, then multiply.
pool.explain: k = 3, so B's opposite side is 9. Then 9 ÷ 15 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Size does not change sin θ.

pool.prompt: In triangle PQR the right angle is at R and θ is at Q. What is cos θ?
pool.hint: Hypotenuse: opposite the right angle. Adjacent: touches Q and is not the hypotenuse.
pool.explain: PQ is the hypotenuse and QR is adjacent to θ, so cos θ = QR/PQ. PR/PQ is sin θ.

pool.prompt: A right triangle has opposite {=3*k}, adjacent {=4*k} and hypotenuse {=5*k}. What is sin θ as a decimal?
pool.explain: {=3*k} ÷ {=5*k} = 0.6, the same as 3 ÷ 5. The {k} cancels, whatever size the triangle is.

pool.prompt: Kai says: 'sin 20° ≈ 0.342, so sin 40° ≈ 0.684.' Is he right?
choices: No: sin 40° ≈ 0.643, because sine is not proportional to the angle
Yes: double the angle, double the sine
pool.hint: Draw both triangles with hypotenuse 10. Does the opposite side double?
pool.explain: sin 40° ≈ 0.643. The ratio grows with the angle, but more and more slowly, so doubling θ does not double sin θ.

pool.prompt: Which of these can never be bigger than 1?
choices: sin θ, since the hypotenuse is the longest side
tan θ, since it uses the two shorter sides
Neither of them can be bigger than 1
pool.hint: Which ratio has the longest side on the bottom?
pool.explain: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, and the hypotenuse is longest, so sin θ < 1. tan 60° ≈ 1.73, so tan can be bigger than 1.

pool.prompt: Two right triangles share an angle θ. The small one has adjacent {a} cm and hypotenuse {h} cm. The big one has adjacent {=a*k} cm. How long is its hypotenuse?
pool.hint: Scale factor = {=a*k} ÷ {a}. Multiply the hypotenuse by it.
pool.explain: k = {k}, so the hypotenuse is {h} × {k} = {=h*k} cm, and cos θ stays {a}/{h}.

items: Move θ to the other sharp corner
